executive_assessment.text: Freetown wards and Western Area sites add local flood/landslide exposure, while district health-system and drought findings rely on dated inputs and projections.

Conflict-era migration adds historical Freetown water pressure. Border peacebuilding and WFP summaries identify capacity and sustainability issues without establishing climate-caused violence or independent causal resilience gains.

geographic_notes.text: The climate-health assessment maps Freetown flood-risk channels and identifies Lumley, Juba, Susan's Bay and Regent as highest flood-fatality-risk wards; estimates use older modeling inputs, not current annual casualties.

Source dated 2024 reports: For the 2050 s, Koinadugu, Kono and Kailahun are projected to be the districts most vulnerable to drought, although the assessment estimates low countrywide likelihood of severe drought.

Source dated 2024 reports: A 2017 hazard system identified 81 of 1,317 health facilities at flood-inundation risk; Kailahun and Bombali had none, while Koinadugu had low reported health-worker density.

Source dated 2024 reports: The government risk profile identifies Leicester, Regent, Granville Brook, Cline Town, Moa Wharf, Hill Court Road, Kissy Brook, Dwarzark and Charlotte in Western Area as landslide-prone under steep slopes and wet-season heavy rain.

Source dated 2024 reports: The strategy reports that 2015 and 2017 floods and landslides affected nearly 20,000 people and killed 1,141; 2017 Freetown events caused estimated damages of US$16.8 million and losses of US$14.9 million.
The 2023 CCA describes conflict-era and subsequent migration adding pressure to Freetown water resources, alongside separate rainfall-related flow reductions.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 17 of 17 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
Sierra Leone's direct-climate-FCV material is qualitative NDC risk framing; no measured causal effect or localized conflict-climate dataset was inspected.
The CCDR notes substantial rainfall projection uncertainty; its poverty results are scenario-dependent rather than forecasts of observed outcomes.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The subnational climate-health and facility evidence uses dated inputs, including 2017 facility exposure and 2016 workforce tables; current district-level monitoring was not located.

No accessible source found in the targeted searches documenting organized violence or insecurity halting a named climate-adaptation operation. Absence of such evidence in these searches is not evidence that disruption never occurs.
The UN CCA describes conflict-era rural migration and climate-related water stress in Freetown but does not estimate a causal relationship between climate change and conflict.
The 2026 farmer-herder study's full journal paper and the detailed WFP evaluation PDF were inaccessible; claims are limited to fully read publisher/institution summaries.
The WFP evaluation webpage date conflicts with its stated fieldwork period; the underlying report date and detailed evaluation evidence could not be independently reconciled.
The climate-health PDF has 2023 copyright while its filename labels 2024; an exact publication year is left unnormalized.
WFP's displayed 2023 page date predates its stated 2023-2024 fieldwork; its findings remain summary-only with unresolved report dating.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
